allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 十二月，太子長子虨病，太子為虨求王爵，不許。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: In the twelfth month the heir apparent's eldest son Sima Xian fell ill. The heir apparent asked that he be made a prince, but the request was denied.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: In the twelfth month the Heir Apparent's eldest son Sima Xian fell ill; the Heir Apparent sought a princely title for Xian but was not granted it.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 虨疾篤，太子為之禱祀求福。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: As Xian grew gravely ill, the heir apparent prayed and offered sacrifices on his behalf.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: When Xian's illness grew grave, the Heir Apparent prayed and offered sacrifices to seek blessing for him.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 賈后聞之，乃詐稱帝不豫，召太子入朝，既至，后不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞以帝命賜太子酒三升，使盡飲之。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Empress Jia heard of this and falsely announced that the emperor was ill, summoning the heir apparent to court. When he arrived she refused to see him, placed him in a side room, and sent the maid Chen Wu with the emperor's name to give him three pints of wine and order him to drink it all.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: When Empress Jia heard of it she falsely announced the emperor was unwell and summoned the Heir Apparent to court; once he arrived the empress did not see him but placed him in a separate room and sent the maid Chen Wu, in the emperor's name, to bestow three pints of wine on the Heir Apparent and order him to drink it all.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 太子辭以不能飲三升，舞逼之曰：「不孝邪！
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: He declined, saying he could not drink so much. Wu pressed him: "Are you unfilial?
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: The Heir Apparent declined, saying he could not drink three pints; Wu pressed him: "Are you unfilial!

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 天賜汝酒而不飲，酒中有惡物邪！」
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Heaven grants you wine and you refuse. Do you think it poisoned?"
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Heaven bestows wine upon you and you will not drink—is there something evil in the wine!"

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 太子不得已，強飲至盡，遂大醉。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Unable to refuse further, he drank it all and became thoroughly drunk.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: The Heir Apparent had no choice, forced himself to drink to the end, and became very drunk.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 后使黃門侍朗潘岳作書草，令小婢承福，以紙筆及草，因太子醉，稱詔使書之，文曰：「陛下宜自了，不自了，吾當入了之。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: The empress had Pan Yue, Yellow Gate Attendant, draft a letter and sent the maid Cheng Fu with paper, brush, and draft. While the heir apparent was drunk she claimed an imperial order and made him copy it. The text read: "Your Majesty ought to settle this yourself. If you do not, I shall enter and settle it.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: The empress had the Yellow Gate Attendant Pan Yue draft a letter, ordered the little maid Cheng Fu to bring paper, brush, and draft; taking advantage of the Heir Apparent's drunkenness she claimed an edict and made him write it. The text read: "Your Majesty ought to settle matters yourself; if you do not settle them, I shall enter and settle them.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 中宮又宜速自了，不自了，吾當手了之。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: The empress too ought quickly to settle matters herself. If she does not, I shall settle them with my own hand.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: The central palace too ought quickly to settle matters herself; if she does not, I shall settle them with my own hand.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 並與謝妃共要，刻期兩發，勿疑猶豫，以致後患。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: I have agreed with Consort Xie. We have set a date for both to act. Do not hesitate and bring later trouble.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Together with Consort Xie we have agreed; set a date for both to act—do not doubt or hesitate and bring later trouble.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 茹毛飲血於三辰之下，皇天許當掃除患害，立道文為王，蔣氏為內主。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood under heaven. August Heaven has promised to sweep away the harm, establish Daowen as king, and make the Jiang clan the inner mistress.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Eating raw flesh and drinking blood beneath the three luminaries—August Heaven has promised to sweep away the harm, establish Daowen as king, and make the Jiang clan the inner mistress.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 願成，當三牲祠北君。」
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: When it succeeds, we shall offer the three sacrificial beasts to the Northern Lord."
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: When the wish is fulfilled, we shall offer the three sacrificial beasts to the Northern Lord."

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 太子醉迷不覺，遂依而寫之。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Drunk and unaware, he copied it as dictated.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: The Heir Apparent, drunk and dazed and unaware, thereupon copied it as given.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 其字半不成，后補成之，以呈帝。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Half the characters were incomplete. The empress finished them and presented the letter to the emperor.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Half his characters were incomplete; the empress completed them and presented it to the emperor.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 賈后使董猛矯以長廣公主辭白帝曰：「事宜速決，而群臣各不同，其不從詔者，宜以軍法從事。」
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Empress Jia had Dong Meng report to the emperor in the name of the Princess of Changguang: "This must be decided at once. The ministers are divided. Those who disobey the edict should be dealt with by military law."
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Empress Jia had Dong Meng, falsely in the name of the Princess of Changguang, report to the emperor: "The affair ought to be decided quickly, yet the ministers all differ; those who do not follow the edict ought to be handled by military law."

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 議至日西，不決。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Debate continued until sunset without resolution.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Deliberation continued until the sun was in the west, without decision.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 后見華等意堅，懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Seeing Zhang Hua and the others hold firm and fearing the plot might fail, the empress memorialized to depose the heir apparent as a commoner. The edict was approved.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: The empress, seeing that Hua and the others were firm in intent and fearing the affair might change, submitted a memorial to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner; an edict approved it.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 於是使尚書和郁等持節詣東宮，廢太子為庶人，太子改服出，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車，車武公澹以兵仗送太子及妃王氏、三子虨、臧、尚同幽於金墉城。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace. The heir apparent changed his garments, bowed twice, received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart. Sima Dan, Marquis of Chewu, escorted him with armed guards, together with his consort Lady Wang and his three sons Xian, Zang, and Shang, to confinement at Jinyong.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Thereupon He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner. The Heir Apparent changed his garments and came out, bowed twice and received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, rode a rough ox-cart, and the Marquis of Chewu, Sima Dan, with arms escorted the Heir Apparent, his consort Lady Wang, and his three sons Xian, Zang, and Shang together to be confined at Jinyong.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 王衍自表離婚，許之，妃慟哭而歸。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Wang Yan memorialized to divorce her, and permission was granted. The consort returned home in bitter tears.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Wang Yan himself submitted a memorial requesting divorce; it was granted, and the consort returned home weeping bitterly.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 殺太子母謝淑媛及虨母保林蔣俊。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: The heir apparent's mother, Lady Xie the Gracious Lady, and Xian's mother, Forest Keeper Jiang Jun, were executed.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: The Heir Apparent's mother, the Gracious Lady Xie, and Xian's mother, the Forest Keeper Jiang Jun, were killed.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 丙子，皇孫虨卒。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: On the day bingzi the imperial grandson Xian died.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: On the day bingzi the imperial grandson Xian died.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 秀因使人行反間，言殿中人欲廢皇后，迎太子。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Xiu spread disinformation that palace insiders meant to depose the empress and restore the heir apparent.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Xiu therefore sent men to spread counter-intelligence, saying those in the palace wished to depose the empress and welcome the Heir Apparent.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 賈后數遣宮婢微服於民間聽察，聞之甚懼。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: The empress often sent maids in disguise to listen among the people and was terrified.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Empress Jia often sent palace maids in plain dress among the people to listen; hearing this she was greatly afraid.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 倫、秀因勸謐等早除太子，以絕眾望。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Lun and Xiu urged Mi and others to kill the heir apparent at once and end public hope.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Lun and Xiu therefore urged Mi and the rest to eliminate the Heir Apparent early and cut off public hope.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 癸未，賈后使太醫令程據和毒藥。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: On guimao the empress had Cheng Ju, Director of Imperial Physicians, prepare poison.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: On the day guimao Empress Jia had the Director of Imperial Physicians Cheng Ju compound poison.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 矯詔使黃門孫慮至許昌毒太子。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: A forged edict sent Sun Lv of the Yellow Gate to Xuchang to poison the heir apparent.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: A forged edict sent the Yellow Gate Sun Lv to Xuchang to poison the Heir Apparent.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 太子自廢黜，恐被毒，常自煮食於前；
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Since his deposition he feared poison and often cooked for himself;
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Since his deposition the Heir Apparent feared poison and often cooked his own food beforehand;

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子於小坊中，絕其食，宮人猶竊於牆上過食與之。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Lv told Liu Zhen, who moved him to a small compound and cut off food, though palace women still passed food over the wall.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Lv reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen then moved the Heir Apparent to a small compound and cut off his food, yet palace women still secretly passed food over the wall.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 慮逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，慮以藥杵椎殺之。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Lv forced the drug on him; he refused; Lv beat him to death with the pestle.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Lv forced the Heir Apparent to take the drug; he refused; Lv killed him with the drug pestle.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 有司請以庶人禮葬，賈后表請以廣陵王禮葬之。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Officials requested commoner burial; the empress asked for princely rites as for the Prince of Guangling.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: The authorities requested burial with commoner rites; the empress memorialized for burial with the rites of a Prince of Guangling.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 於是趙王倫稱詔赦天下，自為使持節、都督中外諸軍事、相國、侍中，一依宣、文輔魏故事。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Lun proclaimed amnesty, made himself Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief, Chancellor, and Attendant, following the precedents of the Sima regents of Wei.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Thereupon the Prince of Zhao Lun proclaimed an edict amnestying the realm, made himself Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs, Chancellor, and Attendant, following the precedents of Xuan and Wen in assisting Wei.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 置府兵萬人，以其世子散騎常侍荂領冗從僕射，子馥為前將軍，封濟陽王；
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: He stationed ten thousand household troops; his heir Fu, Regular Attendant, held redundant Follower posts; son Fu was Forward General, Prince of Jiyang;
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: He stationed ten thousand troops at his headquarters; his heir, Regular Attendant Within the Encampment Fu, held redundant Followers as Vice-Director; his son Fu was Forward General and Prince of Jiyang;

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 虔為黃門朗，封汝陰王；
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Qian was Yellow Gate Gentleman, Prince of Runan;
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Qian was Yellow Gate Gentleman, Prince of Runan;

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 詡為散騎侍郎，封霸城侯。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Xu was Gentleman of the Encampment, Marquis of Bacheng.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Xu was Gentleman of the Encampment, Marquis of Bacheng.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 孫秀等皆封大郡，並據兵權，文武官封侯者數千人，百官總己以聽於倫。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Sun Xiu and others received great fiefs and military power; thousands of officials were enfeoffed; all offices reported to Lun.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Sun Xiu and the rest were all enfeoffed in great commanderies and held military power; civil and military officials enfeoffed as marquis numbered in the thousands; the hundred offices all reported to Lun.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 倫素庸愚，復受制於孫秀。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Lun was mediocre and foolish and controlled by Sun Xiu.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Lun was by nature mediocre and foolish and again controlled by Sun Xiu.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 秀為中書令，威權振朝廷，天下皆事秀而無求於倫。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Xiu became Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; power radiated from him; the realm served Xiu, not Lun.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Xiu was Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; his authority shook the court; the realm served Xiu and sought nothing from Lun.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 詔追復故太子遹位號，使尚書和郁帥東宮官屬迎太子喪於許昌，追封遹子虨為南陽王，封虨弟臧為臨淮王，尚為襄陽王。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: An edict restored Yu's title, sent He Yu to bring the coffin from Xuchang, posthumously enfeoffed Xian as Prince of Nanyang and brothers Zang and Shang as princes.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: An edict restored the former Heir Apparent Yu's title and rank, sent the Masters of Writing He Yu leading Eastern Palace officials to meet the Heir Apparent's coffin at Xuchang, posthumously enfeoffed Yu's son Xian as Prince of Nanyang, and enfeoffed Xian's brothers Zang as Prince of Linhuai and Shang as Prince of Xiangyang.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 中護軍淮南王允，性沉毅，宿衛將士皆畏服之。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Yun, Prince of Huainan, Central Protector of the Army, was deep and resolute by nature, and the palace guards all feared him.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: The Central Protector of the Army, the Prince of Huainan Yun, was by nature deep and resolute; the garrison soldiers all feared and submitted to him.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 允知相國倫及孫秀有異志，陰養死士，謀討之；
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Knowing Lun and Xiu meant to rebel, he secretly gathered men willing to die and plotted against them;
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Yun knew Chancellor Lun and Sun Xiu harbored rebellious intent and secretly nurtured men willing to die, plotting to attack them;

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 倫、秀深憚之。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Lun and Xiu feared him deeply.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Lun and Xiu deeply dreaded him.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 秋，八月，轉允為太尉，外示優崇，實奪其兵權。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: In autumn, the eighth month, he was transferred to Grand Commandant, an outward honor that in fact stripped him of military command.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Yun was transferred to Grand Commandant—outwardly a mark of honor, in reality his military power was taken away.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 允稱疾不拜。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: He pleaded illness and refused the appointment.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Yun pleaded illness and would not accept the appointment.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 秀遣御史劉機逼允，收其官屬以下，劾以拒詔，大逆不敬。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Xiu sent Censor Liu Ji to coerce him, arrested his staff, and charged him with resisting an edict and great impiety.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Xiu sent the Censor Liu Ji to press Yun, seized his officials and subordinates, and impeached him for resisting an edict, great irreverence and impiety.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 允視詔，乃秀手書也，大怒，收御史，將斬之，御史走免，斬其令史二人。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Yun saw the edict was in Xiu's own hand, flew into a rage, seized the censor and nearly executed him; the censor fled, and two clerks were beheaded.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Yun looked at the edict—it was in Xiu's own hand—and grew greatly angry, seized the censor, and was about to behead him; the censor fled and escaped, and two clerks were beheaded.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 厲色謂左右曰：「趙王欲破我家！」
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: He said grimly to his attendants: "The Prince of Zhao means to destroy my house!"
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: With stern countenance he said to those at his side: "The Prince of Zhao means to destroy my house!"

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 遂帥國兵及帳下七百人直出，大呼曰：「趙王反，我將討之，從我者左袒。」
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: He led his state troops and seven hundred household guards straight out, shouting: "The Prince of Zhao has rebelled! I shall punish him. Follow me and bare your left shoulder."
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: He thereupon led his state troops and seven hundred men of his personal guard straight out, shouting loudly: "The Prince of Zhao has rebelled—I shall punish him; those who follow me, bare your left shoulder."

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 於是歸之者甚眾。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Many rallied to him.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: At this very many came over to him.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 允將赴宮，尚書左丞王輿閉掖門，允不得入，遂圍相府。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Yun marched on the palace, but Wang Yu, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, shut the side gate and blocked him; he then besieged the chancellor's residence.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Yun was about to go to the palace; the Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yu closed the side gate, and Yun could not enter; he thereupon besieged the chancellor's mansion.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 允所將兵皆精銳，倫與戰，屢敗，死者千餘人。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Yun's troops were elite. Lun fought him repeatedly and lost, with more than a thousand dead.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: The troops Yun led were all elite; Lun fought him and was repeatedly defeated, more than a thousand dead.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 太子左率陳徽勒東宮兵，鼓噪於內以應允。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Chen Hui, Colonel of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent, stirred Eastern Palace troops to cheer within in support of Yun.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Chen Hui, Colonel of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent, roused Eastern Palace troops and clamored within in support of Yun.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 允結陳於承華門前，弓弩齊發，射倫，飛矢雨下。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Yun formed battle lines before the Chenghua Gate. Bows and crossbows volleyed at Lun until arrows fell like rain.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Yun drew up his array before the Chenghua Gate; bows and crossbows fired together, shooting at Lun—arrows fell like rain.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 主書司馬眭秘以身蔽倫，箭中其背而死。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Chief Clerk Sima Sui shielded Lun with his body and was killed by an arrow in the back.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: The Chief Clerk Sima Sui shielded Lun with his body; an arrow struck his back and he died.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 倫官屬皆隱樹而立，每樹輒中數百箭，自辰至未，中書令陳淮，徽之兄也，欲應允，言於帝曰：「宜遣白虎幡以解鬥。」
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Lun's staff hid behind trees, each tree studded with hundreds of arrows. From chen to wei, Chen Huai, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Hui's elder brother, wished to aid Yun and told the emperor: "Send the white tiger banner to stop the fighting."
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Lun's staff all hid behind trees to stand; each tree received hundreds of arrows. From the hour chen to wei, the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Chen Huai—Hui's elder brother—wished to support Yun and said to the emperor: "The white tiger banner should be sent to halt the fighting."

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 乃使司馬督護伏胤將騎四百持幡從宮中出。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: The Major of the Protectorate Fu Yin was sent with four hundred horsemen bearing the banner from the palace.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: He then had the Major Fu Yin of the Protectorate lead four hundred horsemen bearing the banner out from within the palace.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 侍中汝陰王虔在門下省，陰與胤誓曰：「富貴當與卿共之。」
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: The Attendant, Prince of Runan Qian, was in the Gate Department and secretly swore to Yin: "We shall share wealth and honor."
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: The Attendant, the Prince of Runan Qian, was in the Gate Department; he secretly swore with Yin: "Wealth and honor shall be shared with you."

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 胤乃懷空板出，詐言有詔助淮南王。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Yin carried out a blank tablet and falsely claimed an edict to aid the Prince of Huainan.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Yin then carried a blank tablet out and falsely said there was an edict to aid the Prince of Huainan.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 允不之覺，開陣內之，下車受詔；
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Yun did not detect the fraud and opened his ranks. Yin dismounted to receive the edict;
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Yun did not perceive the deception and opened his ranks to admit him; Yin dismounted to receive the edict;

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 胤因殺之，並殺允子秦王郁、漢王迪，坐允夷滅者數千人。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Yin then killed him, along with Yun's sons Yu, Prince of Qin, and Di, Prince of Han. Several thousand connected with Yun were exterminated.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Yin thereupon killed him, and also killed Yun's sons, the Prince of Qin Yu and the Prince of Han Di; those implicated with Yun and exterminated numbered several thousand.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 曲赦洛陽。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: A partial amnesty was granted to Luoyang.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: A partial amnesty was granted to Luoyang.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 初，孫秀嘗為小吏，事黃門郎潘岳，岳屢撻之。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Earlier Xiu had served as a petty clerk under Pan Yue, Yellow Gate Gentleman, whom he had often flogged.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Earlier Sun Xiu had once been a petty clerk serving the Yellow Gate Gentleman Pan Yue; Yue often flogged him.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 衛尉石崇之甥歐陽建素與相國倫有隙，崇有愛妾曰綠珠，孫秀便求之，崇不與。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Ouyang Jian, nephew of Commandant of the Guards Shi Chong, was estranged from Lun. Chong had a beloved concubine, Green Pearl, whom Xiu demanded and Chong refused.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Ouyang Jian, nephew of the Commandant of the Guards Shi Chong, had long been at odds with Chancellor Lun; Chong had a beloved concubine named Green Pearl whom Sun Xiu asked for, but Chong would not give her.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 及淮南王允敗，秀因稱石崇、潘岳、歐陽建奉允為亂，收之。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: When Yun fell, Xiu accused Chong, Yue, and Jian of supporting his rebellion and arrested them.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: When the Prince of Huainan Yun was defeated, Xiu thereupon claimed that Shi Chong, Pan Yue, and Ouyang Jian supported Yun in rebellion and arrested them.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 崇歎曰：「奴輩利吾財爾！」
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Chong sighed: "These slaves want my wealth!"
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Chong sighed: "These slaves covet my wealth!"

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 收者曰：「知財為禍，何不早散之？」
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: The arresters said: "If wealth brings disaster, why not have given it away?"
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: The arresters said: "Knowing wealth brings disaster, why not have dispersed it early?"

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 崇不能答。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Chong had no answer.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Chong could not answer.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 初，潘岳母常誚責岳曰：「汝當知足，而乾沒不已乎！」
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Earlier Yue's mother had often scolded him: "Know when you have enough—why keep grasping for more?"
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Earlier Pan Yue's mother often reproached Yue, saying: "You ought to know sufficiency—why seize and scrape without end!"

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 及敗，岳謝母曰：「負阿母。」
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: When ruin came Yue told his mother: "I have failed you, Mother."
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: When disaster came Yue apologized to his mother: "I have failed you, Mother."

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 遂與崇，建皆族誅，籍沒崇家。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Yue, Chong, and Jian were executed to the clan, and Chong's estate was confiscated.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Thereupon Yue, Chong, and Jian were all executed to the clan, and Chong's property was confiscated.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 相國倫收淮南王母弟吳王晏，欲殺之。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Lun arrested Yan, Prince of Wu, younger brother of Yun's mother, intending to kill him.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Chancellor Lun arrested the Prince of Wu Yan, younger brother of the Prince of Huainan's mother, intending to kill him.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 光祿大夫傅祗爭之於朝堂，眾皆諫止倫，倫乃貶晏為賓徒縣王。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Household Grandee Fu Zhi argued for him in court; all remonstrated, and Lun degraded Yan to Prince of Bintu.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: The Household Grandee Fu Zhi contended for him in the court hall; all remonstrated and stopped Lun, and Lun thereupon degraded Yan to Prince of Bintu county.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 廞自稱大都督，大將軍、益州牧，署置僚屬，改易守令。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Xin styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, and Governor of Yi, appointed staff, and replaced local officials.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Xin styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, and Governor of Yi Province, appointed staff, and changed the garrison commanders and magistrates.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 王官被召，無敢不往。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: When court officials were summoned, none dared refuse.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: When court officials were summoned none dared not go.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 李庠帥妹婿李含、天水任回、上官昌、扶風李攀、始平費他、氐苻成、隗伯等四千騎歸廞。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Li Xiu led Li Han, Ren Hui, Shangguan Chang, Li Pan, Fei Ta, Fu Cheng, Wei Bo, and four thousand horsemen to join Xin.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Li Xiu led his brothers-in-law Li Han of Tianshui, Ren Hui, Shangguan Chang, Li Pan of Fufeng, Fei Ta of Shiping, the Di Fu Cheng, and Wei Bo and others with four thousand horsemen to join Xin.

allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.zh: 廞以庠為威寇將軍，封陽泉亭侯，委以心膂，使招合六郡壯勇至萬餘人，以斷北道。
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.en: Xin made Li Xiang General Who Subdues Bandits and Marquis of Yangquan, trusted him deeply, and had him gather more than ten thousand braves of six commanderies to block the northern road.
allPrimaryGoverningBlocks.literal: Xin made Li Xiang General Who Subdues Bandits and Marquis of Yangquan Pavilion, entrusted him as close confidant, and had him gather braves of the six commanderies to more than ten thousand to cut the northern road.

allChineseBin.zh: 十二月，太子長子虨病，太子為虨求王爵，不許。
allChineseBin.en: In the twelfth month the heir apparent's eldest son Sima Xian fell ill. The heir apparent asked that he be made a prince, but the request was denied.
allChineseBin.literal: In the twelfth month the Heir Apparent's eldest son Sima Xian fell ill; the Heir Apparent sought a princely title for Xian but was not granted it.

allChineseBin.zh: 虨疾篤，太子為之禱祀求福。
allChineseBin.en: As Xian grew gravely ill, the heir apparent prayed and offered sacrifices on his behalf.
allChineseBin.literal: When Xian's illness grew grave, the Heir Apparent prayed and offered sacrifices to seek blessing for him.

allChineseBin.zh: 於是使尚書和郁等持節詣東宮，廢太子為庶人，太子改服出，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車，車武公澹以兵仗送太子及妃王氏、三子虨、臧、尚同幽於金墉城。
allChineseBin.en: He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace. The heir apparent changed his garments, bowed twice, received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart. Sima Dan, Marquis of Chewu, escorted him with armed guards, together with his consort Lady Wang and his three sons Xian, Zang, and Shang, to confinement at Jinyong.
allChineseBin.literal: Thereupon He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner. The Heir Apparent changed his garments and came out, bowed twice and received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, rode a rough ox-cart, and the Marquis of Chewu, Sima Dan, with arms escorted the Heir Apparent, his consort Lady Wang, and his three sons Xian, Zang, and Shang together to be confined at Jinyong.

allChineseBin.zh: 殺太子母謝淑媛及虨母保林蔣俊。
allChineseBin.en: The heir apparent's mother, Lady Xie the Gracious Lady, and Xian's mother, Forest Keeper Jiang Jun, were executed.
allChineseBin.literal: The Heir Apparent's mother, the Gracious Lady Xie, and Xian's mother, the Forest Keeper Jiang Jun, were killed.

allChineseBin.en: On the day bingzi the imperial grandson Xian died.
allChineseBin.literal: On the day bingzi the imperial grandson Xian died.

allChineseBin.zh: 詔追復故太子遹位號，使尚書和郁帥東宮官屬迎太子喪於許昌，追封遹子虨為南陽王，封虨弟臧為臨淮王，尚為襄陽王。
allChineseBin.en: An edict restored Yu's title, sent He Yu to bring the coffin from Xuchang, posthumously enfeoffed Xian as Prince of Nanyang and brothers Zang and Shang as princes.
allChineseBin.literal: An edict restored the former Heir Apparent Yu's title and rank, sent the Masters of Writing He Yu leading Eastern Palace officials to meet the Heir Apparent's coffin at Xuchang, posthumously enfeoffed Yu's son Xian as Prince of Nanyang, and enfeoffed Xian's brothers Zang as Prince of Linhuai and Shang as Prince of Xiangyang.

allZhongshuLing.zh: 秀為中書令，威權振朝廷，天下皆事秀而無求於倫。
allZhongshuLing.en: Xiu became Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; power radiated from him; the realm served Xiu, not Lun.
allZhongshuLing.literal: Xiu was Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; his authority shook the court; the realm served Xiu and sought nothing from Lun.

allZhongshuLing.zh: 倫官屬皆隱樹而立，每樹輒中數百箭，自辰至未，中書令陳淮，徽之兄也，欲應允，言於帝曰：「宜遣白虎幡以解鬥。」
allZhongshuLing.en: Lun's staff hid behind trees, each tree studded with hundreds of arrows. From chen to wei, Chen Huai, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Hui's elder brother, wished to aid Yun and told the emperor: "Send the white tiger banner to stop the fighting."
allZhongshuLing.literal: Lun's staff all hid behind trees to stand; each tree received hundreds of arrows. From the hour chen to wei, the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Chen Huai—Hui's elder brother—wished to support Yun and said to the emperor: "The white tiger banner should be sent to halt the fighting."

allBaolin.zh: 殺太子母謝淑媛及虨母保林蔣俊。
allBaolin.en: The heir apparent's mother, Lady Xie the Gracious Lady, and Xian's mother, Forest Keeper Jiang Jun, were executed.
allBaolin.literal: The Heir Apparent's mother, the Gracious Lady Xie, and Xian's mother, the Forest Keeper Jiang Jun, were killed.

allGuiwei.zh: 癸未，賈后使太醫令程據和毒藥。
allGuiwei.en: On guimao the empress had Cheng Ju, Director of Imperial Physicians, prepare poison.
allGuiwei.literal: On the day guimao Empress Jia had the Director of Imperial Physicians Cheng Ju compound poison.

allLiXiang.en: Li Xiu led Li Han, Ren Hui, Shangguan Chang, Li Pan, Fei Ta, Fu Cheng, Wei Bo, and four thousand horsemen to join Xin.
allLiXiang.literal: Li Xiu led his brothers-in-law Li Han of Tianshui, Ren Hui, Shangguan Chang, Li Pan of Fufeng, Fei Ta of Shiping, the Di Fu Cheng, and Wei Bo and others with four thousand horsemen to join Xin.

otherSameEnglishOfficeWordingDifferentCh.en: An edict ordered arrest of the Jia clan; the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and Eight Seats were summoned at night.
otherSameEnglishOfficeWordingDifferentCh.literal: An edict ordered the Masters of Writing to arrest the Jia kin; the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and the Eight Seats were all summoned into the hall at night.

Xin made Li Xiang General Who Subdues Bandits and Marquis of Yangquan Pavilion, entrusted him as close confidant, and had him gather braves of the six commanderies to more than ten thousand to cut the northern road.

In the continuous Zhao Xin frame, s0385 explicitly names 李庠 joining 廞, then s0386 廞以庠 appoints that same Li Xiang. 孫秀 belongs to the separate s0354 empress episode. Accept only the proposed Xiu to Li Xiang replacement in this field; no date or other wording change is approved.
